payload.function_structure:
SECOND FILL. Inherits F1-F28 unchanged — they were solution-neutral and survive the rewalk. SEVEN ADDED (F29-F35), all from the review-and-promotion requirements the first pass did not have. Use-case coverage re-mapped onto the current ten use cases.

OVERALL FUNCTION: supply the worker with what it needs to work correctly, decide mechanically what can be decided, and make the worker answer for the rest.
(The first pass's overall function stopped at the second clause. The third is what the rewalk added, and it is the one the whole iteration turns on.)

Solution-neutral throughout — no tool named, because M4 chooses the tools.

F-GROUP 1: ACQUIRE MATERIAL
- F1 locate material (find where something is, by pattern, by shape of name, or by absence)
- F2 deliver material in portions (hand over a requested part, and say how much remains)
- F3 reach material outside the immediate workspace
- F4 reach material that exists only in the record
- F5 bound the retrieval (limit time, quantity and width)
- F6 contain the reach (keep an addressed source addressable and nothing beyond it)

F-GROUP 2: ANSWER HONESTLY
- F7 refuse a malformed request (decline rather than infer a missing part)
- F8 report absence
- F9 report incompleteness (say what was not delivered, never imply wholeness)

F-GROUP 3: ALTER MATERIAL
- F10 alter many places as one act
- F11 guard each alteration
- F12 undo the whole on any failure
- F13 keep alteration to one path

F-GROUP 4: SUPPLY THE RULES
- F14 select the rules that bind this work (choose by declared applicability)
- F15 resolve a rule to its content (deliver the rule itself, not a pointer to it)
- F16 report the weight of what was supplied
- F29 EXPOSE A RULE THAT BINDS NOBODY (find the rule that declares no applicability, so an incomplete set cannot look complete)

F-GROUP 5: DECIDE MECHANICALLY
- F17 derive a fact from the record
- F18 compare a fact against what is claimed
- F19 hand back what cannot be decided (defer without stopping)
- F20 state the fact behind a refusal
- F21 distinguish decided from claimed
- F30 REFUSE A PROOF THAT PROVED NOTHING (treat an empty demonstration as failure, never as success)

F-GROUP 6: PRESERVE THE RECORD
- F22 name the record immutably
- F23 name the record readably
- F24 remove competing names
- F25 carry the names outward
- F31 PRESERVE WHAT WAS SUPERSEDED (keep a claim that did not survive, marked as not surviving)

F-GROUP 7: HOLD LOCAL SETTINGS
- F26 present settings (without exposing what must stay secret)
- F27 accept and validate settings

F-GROUP 8: ACCOUNT FOR ACCESS
- F28 record what was consulted

F-GROUP 9: OBLIGE THE REVIEW (new — the milestone the first pass had no functions for)
- F32 DEMAND THE REVIEW (require the examination as part of the work, not beside it)
- F33 RETURN WORK TO AN EARLIER POINT (re-open what a judgement rejected, together with everything derived from it)
- F34 KEEP THE RETURNED PATH TRAVERSABLE (ensure work sent back can reach its judgement again)
- F35 WITHDRAW A STANDING DECISION (revoke an offer whose basis was rejected, wherever it is showing)

F-GROUP 10: SHARE THE JUDGE (new)
- F36 DELIVER A CHANGED RULE-KEEPER TO EVERY WORKER (make one worker's improvement to the shared judge available to all of them, or to none)

SEPARATIONS THAT ARE DELIBERATE AND LOAD-BEARING, four now:
- F22 apart from F23. An immutable name and a readable name are different jobs; conflating them is the defect where a deletable label is the only pointer.
- F18 apart from F19. Deciding and deferring must be distinct outcomes, or 'cannot decide' silently becomes 'fail' and parks a run.
- F33 apart from F34. Returning work and keeping its path open sound like one job and are not. Returning work is easy; the first live return SEVERED the path back, so the work was re-done and could never be re-judged. The machine deadlocked in silence. If these are one function, that failure is invisible by construction.
- F30 apart from F18. Comparing a fact against a claim assumes a fact exists. An examination that produced NO facts is not a passing comparison; it is an absent one, and it reads as success unless something separately refuses it.

NO FUNCTION IS ORPHANED: every one of F1-F36 is required by at least one requirement.

HOLES FOUND AND NAMED rather than papered over. Five steps and two requirements map to NO system function, and every one is a correct boundary rather than a gap:
- UC-A step 5 and UC-A ext 2b — arguing the case against your own conclusion is judgement. A system that generated it would be doing the reviewing, which is precisely the thing that must not be automated away.
- UC-A ext 6c and UC-J steps 1 and 5 — adjudication is a person's act.
- UC-G steps 1-4 — the agent's own writing. R36 constrains it; no function produces it.
- R36 and R38 — both constrain prose or policy rather than capability, which is exactly why both carry verify-by-inspection rather than a test. A function here would be a false mechanism, and R20 exists to stop precisely that kind of unearned label.
- UC-D ext 4a — installing a dependency after the copy rather than before is an ordering obligation inside F36, not a separate function. Recorded because it is the bug that made promotion refuse three times, and someone will later look for the function that prevents it.

WHY THE UNMAPPED ROWS ARE LISTED AT ALL: an unmapped step normally signals a missing function. Here each one signals a deliberate limit of what the machine should do. Left silent, the next reader cannot tell the two apart — and that is the same failure mode as an uncollected rule.
